title: User guide
sub: The DJ mix built on a timeline — free software
intro: TIMELINE DJ MIX builds a complete mix on a timeline: each track is matched to the tempo of the previous one, transitions are shaped with the mouse, then the whole night is exported as a single audio file. The red numbers on the screenshots refer to the lists below them.

p: Windows: run Timeline-DJ-Mix-Windows-Setup.exe. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", click More info, then Run anyway.
macOS: choose the Apple Silicon (M1, M2…) or Intel version, unzip it and drag TIMELINE DJ MIX into Applications. On first launch, open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
Linux: install timeline-dj-mix_amd64.deb (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint) with a double-click, or make the AppImage executable and run it.
Without installing: the file Timeline-DJ-Mix.html opens in Chrome or Edge. It does everything, except keep access to folders from one session to the next.

At the top, the library (left) and the playlist (right). In the middle, the playback line with the sound outputs, then the settings of the selected track. At the bottom, the timeline. The Sound and effects button shows or hides the mixer. Lists at the bottom puts the lists below the timeline; Lists at the top puts them back above. The dividers between areas can be dragged with the mouse, and each area (lists, playback line, Sound and effects) has its own − and + buttons to set its size.

p: Click Import tracks or drop files onto the library: MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, Opus, M4A/AAC and AIFF. The software calculates the BPM, the beat grid and the key, shown with its harmonic wheel code (8A, 9B…).
A green dot marks a key compatible with the track selected in the playlist; a green BPM, a tempo within 6 %. Click a column header to sort, use the search box to filter.
Files stay on your computer; the software keeps a copy so it can find them next time.
Double-click a track, click + or drag it into the playlist. Drag rows to change the order; Sort arranges the tracks by compatible tempo and key.

Each track has its incoming transition: beat-matched fade (both tracks at the same tempo), bass swap (the bass passes from one track to the other in the middle), hard entry, simple fade, no beat-matching (chosen automatically when the tempos are too far apart) or cut.
Tracks alternate on two channels, A (orange) and B (blue). Drag a block to lengthen or shorten the overlap; pull its edges to cut the start or the end. Snap aligns moves to the bar or to the beat.

Click the ruler to place the playhead. Zoom and Show all set the scale; Ctrl + wheel zooms where the mouse is. The orange line at the bottom shows the tempo of the mix, which glides from one track to the next during transitions.
s.cap: The timeline: two channels, overlaps and tempo curve

p: Choose the curve (Volume, Bass or Treble), select a block, then click the curve to add a point and drag it. Double-click a point to delete it. Restore the automatic curves clears the points placed by hand.
s.cap: Bass curve during a bass swap

p: In the track settings: the overlap in beats, the tempo during the transition (glides from one to the other, keeps the outgoing one, takes the incoming one) and the tempo in the mix.
If a track is badly aligned, correct its BPM (÷2, ×2 or exact value), shift the grid by 10 ms, or move the first beat of the bar by one beat. Pitch follows tempo, as on a vinyl turntable.

The ▶ button on each row plays the track in the headphones without stopping the mix, in the library as in the playlist; a slider lets you go anywhere in the track. The ⇄ button plays the transition as it will sound.
The green line on the timeline shows where the mix preview is. Place it by clicking in the bottom strip, Shift + click or right-click, then start Preview.

Outputs are set in the playback line: Output (the mix sound card), the channel layout (Stereo, Master 1-2, headphones 3-4 or Headphones 1-2, master 3-4) and Headphones, to send pre-listening to another sound card. 🔍 shows the card names, ⓘ shows the available channels. With a stereo card, choose Stereo or headphones on another card: otherwise pre-listening is muted so that it never reaches the master output. Changing these settings never interrupts the mix or the pre-listening.

Controller plugged in after start-up: the software detects it and reopens the sound outputs by itself. If the headphones stay silent, click Restart sound card: the audio outputs are reopened without reloading the software, tracks and project stay loaded, and both the mix and the pre-listening resume where they were.

p: For each channel: volume, bass, mids, treble, filter and tempo ±8 %. In the centre, the crossfader; on the right, echo (synced to the tempo), flanger and reverb. Double-click a control to reset it.
Simple view, in the playback line, replaces the knobs with sliders; a green dot lights up when a control is centred. Tick Export to keep these settings in the exported file; ⟲ resets all controls.

s.t: Auto DJ and party by styles
p: Party by styles: add one style per row, choose its folder and the number of tracks per set. The Auto DJ plays, for example, 3 salsas, 3 bachatas, 3 kizombas, then starts again. Build the mix adds the chosen length in one go.
Auto DJ on adds the next track during playback, before the mix ends; the ⏭ button moves to the next style. Without folders, the Auto DJ picks the track closest in tempo and key.
s.cap: Auto DJ and party by styles

p: Choose your device and click Load: mappings from the Mixxx project are read as they are (Pioneer DDJ, Numark, Hercules, Reloop, Allen & Heath, Traktor Kontrol Z1…). Decks 1 and 3 control channel A, decks 2 and 4 channel B, including the tempo fader. Import a Mixxx mapping accepts any other .xml file with its .js files.
To add a command: click Learn on a row, then move the button, knob or fader. A learned command takes priority over the mapping. MIDI works in the installed versions and in Chrome or Edge.
Export the mix renders the whole night into one file: MP3 128, 192 or 320 kbit/s, FLAC 16 or 24-bit, WAV 16 or 24-bit, AIFF. Track list saves the timed list, ready to publish with the mix.
Save the project keeps the order, transitions, curves and tempo corrections in a .json file. Open a project loads it again. The software also keeps the last mix automatically.
↶ undoes (Ctrl + Z) and ↷ redoes (Ctrl + Y), top left, as in a word processor. Editing a waiting track never interrupts the one that is playing.
Colours: background colour (text and panels adapt, even on a light background), button colour and main button colour.

The language is chosen at the top right: French, English, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, German, Greek, Russian, Chinese or Japanese. The change is immediate and kept for next time. Your track titles are never translated.
Space: play / pause · Del: remove the selected track from the mix · Ctrl + Z: undo · Ctrl + Y: redo · Home: back to the start · ← →: back or forward 5 seconds · Ctrl + wheel: timeline zoom.
F1: open this guide in the software's language. It also opens from Help › Full user guide.
Ctrl − and Ctrl +: make the whole display smaller or larger, handy on small screens; Ctrl 0 goes back to 100 %. The A− and A+ buttons, top right, do the same.
Ctrl + wheel over the lists, the playback line or the mixer: size of that area only. Its − and + buttons do the same; a click on its percentage sets it back to 100 %.

TIMELINE DJ MIX is free software (GNU GPL v2 or later), created by DJ LATIN JAZZ & DJ CRISLATINO in collaboration with Claude.ai. A donation on ko-fi.com/djlatinjazz helps it grow. Controller mappings come from the Mixxx project (GPL); MP3 encoding uses lamejs (LGPL).
